unclustered.title: Anthropic’s $15 Billion Credit Line Sets Stage for IPO
unclustered.summary: Anthropic’s anticipated IPO could kick off a busy fall for tech listings after SpaceX dominated the market this summer. Rainmaker Securities co-founder and Managing Director Greg Martin discusses why Anthropic’s planned $15 billion revolving credit facility strengthens its position ahead of a potential offering. He also shares how its rapid growth could support a valuation above SpaceX’s at IPO and why a successful debut could “open the floodgates” for companies including Oura, neoclouds and other long-awaited tech listings. He joins Bloomberg’s Lisa Mateo on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)
unclustered.headline: Anthropic's $15B Credit Line Sets Stage for Blockbuster IPO

unclustered.title: Anthropic Set to Expand Pre-IPO Credit Facility
unclustered.summary: Anthropic PBC is set to finalize an expansion of its revolving credit facility to $15 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, clearing a hurdle before the artificial intelligence firm’s public filing for its highly anticipated IPO. Morgan Stanley is leading the process, the people said. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and JPMorgan Chase & Co. also have prominent roles on the facility, along with Citigroup Inc., they said. The four lenders are also leading the IPO, Bloomberg News has reported. The Claude chatbot maker is seeking to raise as much as SpaceX or more in the initial public offering, people familiar with the preparations have said. Companies typically finalize the revolver before they notify banks of their formal roles in a listing. For more, we speak with Bailey Lipschultz, Senior Equities Reporter for Bloomberg News. (Source: Bloomberg)
unclustered.headline: ANTHROPIC FINALIZING $15B CREDIT LINE BEFORE IPO
